problems.title: A product-to-sum cancellation
problems.question: Simplify $2\sin2\alpha\sin\alpha+\cos3\alpha$.
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
steps: The product is $\cos\alpha-\cos3\alpha$. Adding $\cos3\alpha$ leaves $\cos\alpha$.

problems.title: Period of a scaled sine
problems.question: Find the least positive period of $\pi\sin(2\pi x+3\pi)+4\pi$.
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
steps: Here $k=2\pi$, so $T=1$. Scaling and translating the graph do not change this period.

problems.title: Three double-angle identities
problems.question: Which printed identities expressing $\sin2\alpha,\cos2\alpha,\tan2\alpha$ through $\tan\alpha$ are true?
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
steps: Divide the sine and cosine double-angle formulas by $\cos^2\alpha$ to get the first two. Their quotient gives the third.
All three hold wherever the original expressions are defined.

problems.title: A regular hexagonal prism
problems.question: Base area is 2019 and lateral area 2020. Find base side divided by prism height.
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
steps: The ratio is $2019/(505\sqrt3)=673\sqrt3/505$.

problems.title: Euler’s relation for a prism
problems.question: A prism has $V$ vertices, $I$ edges, $A$ faces. Which printed relation always holds?
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.

problems.title: A sum-to-product quotient
problems.question: Simplify $(\sin\alpha+\sin\beta)/(\cos\alpha+\cos\beta)$.
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
steps: Cancel the common nonzero cosine factor on the original domain. The quotient is the tangent of the half-sum.

problems.title: Symmetric sine factors
problems.question: Simplify $4\sin(60^\circ-\alpha)\sin(60^\circ+\alpha)$.
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
steps: The expression is $4(3/4-\sin^2\alpha)=3-4\sin^2\alpha$.

problems.title: Substitute double-angle values
problems.question: Evaluate $(3\tan2\alpha-5\sin2\alpha)/(3\tan2\alpha+5\cos2\alpha)$ when $\tan\alpha=-2$.
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
steps: The numerator is $4+4=8$ and denominator $4-3=1$.

problems.title: Space diagonals above a rhombus
problems.question: A right parallelepiped has a rhombus base with a $60^\circ$ angle. Its shorter space diagonal equals its longer base diagonal. Find longer space diagonal divided by shorter base diagonal.
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
formulas: For rhombus side $s$, base diagonals are $s,s\sqrt3$; space diagonal squared $=$ base diagonal squared $+h^2$.
steps: The longer space diagonal is $\sqrt{3s^2+2s^2}=s\sqrt5$. Divide by $s$.

problems.title: All diagonal sections of a hexagonal prism
problems.question: A regular hexagonal prism has lateral area 1. Find the sum of areas of all its diagonal sections.
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
formulas: A section through a base diagonal has area $(\text{diagonal})h$.
steps: A regular hexagon has six short diagonals of length $\sqrt3s$ and three long ones of length $2s$.
The area sum is $(6\sqrt3s+6s)h$. Since the lateral area is $6sh=1$, the answer is $\sqrt3+1$.

problems.title: Range of sine on a restricted interval
problems.question: Find the range of $2\sin2x+5$ for $x\in[-\pi/3,\pi/6]$.
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
steps: On this interval sine has minimum $-1$ at $-\pi/2$ and maximum $\sqrt3/2$ at $\pi/3$.
Multiply the range by 2 and add 5.

problems.title: Order four angles
problems.question: $\sin a=\cos b=1/4$, $\tan c=\cot d=-1/4$, with $a,c\in[-\pi/2,\pi/2]$ and $b,d\in[0,\pi]$. Order them.
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
formulas: Sine and tangent are increasing on the stated principal intervals; $\cos b=\sin(\pi/2-b)$.
steps: $c<0<a$. Also $a=\arcsin(1/4)<\pi/4$, while $b=\pi/2-a>\pi/4$.
Negative cotangent with $d\in[0,\pi]$ places $d$ in $(\pi/2,\pi)$, above $b$.

problems.title: A triple-angle quotient
problems.question: Simplify $(\cos7-\cos21)/(\sin^27\cos7)$ (angles in radians).
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
steps: $\cos t-\cos3t=4\cos t(1-\cos^2t)=4\cos t\sin^2t$.
With $t=7$, cancel the nonzero denominator factors to obtain 4.

problems.title: Diagonals of two lateral faces
problems.question: A right prism has an isosceles right triangular base. Its largest lateral face is a square. Find the cosine of the angle between intersecting diagonals of its two smaller lateral faces.
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
steps: Let the base legs be $a,a$. The prism height equals the hypotenuse $a\sqrt2$, since the largest lateral face is square.
At a common vertex the diagonals can be represented by $(a,0,a\sqrt2)$ and $(0,a,a\sqrt2)$. Their dot product is $2a^2$, and each length is $a\sqrt3$.
The cosine is $2a^2/(3a^2)=2/3$.

problems.title: Height from a trapezoidal diagonal section
problems.question: A right prism has an isosceles tangential trapezoid base, base ratio $1:4$, inradius 4, and diagonal-section area 10. Find prism height.
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
formulas: Trapezoid height $=2r=8$; equal legs sum to the bases; section area $=dh$.
steps: Write the bases $a,4a$. Each leg is $5a/2$, with horizontal projection $3a/2$. Pythagoras gives $(5a/2)^2-(3a/2)^2=64$, so $a=4$.
The trapezoid diagonal has horizontal projection 10 and height 8, so its length is $\sqrt{164}=2\sqrt{41}$.
The prism height is $10/(2\sqrt{41})=5/\sqrt{41}$.

problems.title: Square a tangent-cotangent sum
problems.question: $\tan\alpha+\cot\alpha=6$. Find $\tan^2\alpha+\cot^2\alpha$.
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
steps: The value is $36-2=34$.

problems.title: Exact tangents of complementary angles
problems.question: Simplify $\tan75^\circ-\tan15^\circ$.
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
steps: These values simplify to $2+\sqrt3$ and $2-\sqrt3$.
Their difference is $2\sqrt3$.

problems.title: Squared triple-angle ratios
problems.question: Find $\sin^23\alpha/\sin^2\alpha-\cos^23\alpha/\cos^2\alpha$ if $\cos2\alpha=1/8$.
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
steps: Set $c=\cos^2\alpha$. The expression is $(4c-1)^2-(4c-3)^2=16c-8=8\cos2\alpha$.
Substitute $\cos2\alpha=1/8$ to get 1. The nonzero sine and cosine conditions follow from this cosine value.

problems.title: An oblique triangular prism
problems.question: A prism has an equilateral base; one lateral face is square and the other two lateral faces are perpendicular. Find lateral area divided by one base area.
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
formulas: Area of a vector parallelogram $=|u\times v|$; perpendicular planes have perpendicular normals.
steps: Choose $A=(0,0,0),B=(s,0,0),C=(s/2,\sqrt3s/2,0)$. The square face on $AB$ gives lateral edge $v=(0,y,z)$ with $y^2+z^2=s^2$.
Normals to the other two faces have dot product $s^2z^2/2-s^2y^2/4$. Setting it to zero gives $y^2=2z^2$, hence $z^2=s^2/3$.
Each remaining lateral face has area $\sqrt{s^2z^2+s^2y^2/4}=s^2/\sqrt2$. Thus lateral area is $s^2(1+\sqrt2)$. Divide by base area $\sqrt3s^2/4$.

problems.title: Lateral area of a parallelepiped
problems.question: $A_1AD=60^\circ,A_1AB=30^\circ$, $AD=6$, $AB=AA_1=2\sqrt3$. Find lateral area.
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
formulas: Parallelogram area $=ab\sin\theta$; opposite lateral faces have equal areas.
steps: The two distinct face areas are $6(2\sqrt3)\sin60^\circ=18$ and $(2\sqrt3)^2\sin30^\circ=6$.
Double their sum: $L=2(18+6)=48$.

problems.title: A telescoping tangent sum
problems.question: Evaluate the sum of $\sin1^\circ/[\cos(k+1)^\circ\cos k^\circ]$ for $k=1,\ldots,19$.
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
steps: Each summand is $\tan(k+1)^\circ-\tan k^\circ$.
All intermediate terms cancel, leaving $\tan20^\circ-\tan1^\circ$.

problems.title: Three cosines from seventh roots
problems.question: Evaluate $\cos(2\pi/7)+\cos(4\pi/7)+\cos(6\pi/7)$.
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
steps: Take real parts and pair conjugate terms. This gives $1+2[\cos(2\pi/7)+\cos(4\pi/7)+\cos(6\pi/7)]=0$.
The requested sum is $-1/2$.

problems.title: An infinite trigonometric geometric series
problems.question: For $\alpha\notin\pi\mathbb Z$, evaluate $\sin\alpha+\sin\alpha\cos\alpha+\sin\alpha\cos^2\alpha+\cdots$.
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
steps: The restriction ensures $|\cos\alpha|<1$, so the series converges to $\sin\alpha/(1-\cos\alpha)$.
Multiply numerator and denominator by $1+\cos\alpha$ to get $(1+\cos\alpha)/\sin\alpha=\cot(\alpha/2)$.

problems.title: A box diagonal’s angles with its faces
problems.question: A rectangular-box diagonal makes angles $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ with three mutually nonparallel faces. Find the necessary identity.
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
formulas: For diagonal length $d=\sqrt{a^2+b^2+c^2}$, the sine of an angle to a face equals the normal component divided by $d$.
steps: The three sines are $a/d,b/d,c/d$ in some order.
The sum of their squares is $(a^2+b^2+c^2)/d^2=1$.

problems.title: Perpendicular diagonal sections
problems.question: A right parallelepiped has perpendicular diagonal sections of areas 9 and 13. Find its lateral area.
problems.idea: Write the relevant identity or geometric equation before substituting.
formulas: A parallelogram with perpendicular diagonals is a rhombus; side $s=\sqrt{p^2+q^2}/2$.
steps: Let base diagonals be $p,q$ and prism height $h$. The section areas give $ph=9,qh=13$.
Lateral area is $4sh=2\sqrt{(ph)^2+(qh)^2}=2\sqrt{81+169}=10\sqrt{10}$.
